decision: Each tile is a separately built remote mounted at runtime from its manifest
why: Five teams own five systems with different users; they should ship without coordinating a host release.
alternative: Import all five as build-time packages in one bundle.
value: Independent deploys and version isolation, visible on one page.

decision: Every remote runs inside its own error boundary with a designed fallback
why: A remote failing is a normal distributed-systems event; it should cost one system, not all five.
value: Four systems keep working when one is down; Playwright blocks each manifest to prove it.

decision: Remote health and versions come from the manifests themselves
why: The host should report what it can actually load, not what a registry believes is deployed.
value: One source of truth for what is running.

decision: All five remotes share one AI surface contract despite five design languages
why: Trust patterns should be learned once: sparkle, Simulated AI badge, sources, explicit approval.
alternative: Let each team design its own AI UI.
value: Users recognise AI and its limits in every system.
